quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Deer crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that deer cross the road in this area. Slow down, stay alert, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: The posted maximum speed limit is the fastest you can drive in an area.
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: The posted maximum speed limit is the fastest legal speed in an area under ideal conditions. You must slow down when conditions require it, such as wet roads or poor visibility.

questions.question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: First, take your foot off the gas pedal. If you need to slow down more, gently press your brake pedal slowly and steadily.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should turn on high beam headlights to see better.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: In fog, use your low beam headlights or fog lights. High beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see.

questions.question: At night, it is illegal to drive using only parking lights.
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: You must use your headlights when driving at night. Using only parking lights is against the law.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Keep your tires at the correct air pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires slide on water between the tire and road. Low tire pressure, worn tires, and speeding all increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: What happens if a bicyclist doesn't follow traffic laws?

options.text: Bicyclists don't have to follow traffic laws.
They will always get a warning.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can be ticketed.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers. Both can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: School crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a school crossing is ahead.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign means a traffic light is ahead. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: It is illegal to drive next to a motorcycle in the same lane.
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Never share a lane with a motorcycle. Motorcyclists need the full lane width to move safely.

questions.question: You find a vehicle defect that may affect safe operation. What should you do?

options.text: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
Fix the defect when you have the money.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Fix any defect that affects safe operation before driving. Do not wait.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Drive as you would on dry roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead. Your vehicle needs more time to stop.

questions.question: Lanes moving in the same direction are separated by ____ lines.
questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass from either direction.
You can pass from the side with the broken line.
You can pass from the side with the solid line.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the side with the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means passing is allowed from that side. A solid yellow line means passing is not allowed.

questions.question: Before making a right turn, where should your car be?

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Move to the far right side of the road before turning right. Do not cut across other lanes.

questions.question: How do you enter a freeway?

options.text: Signal, let other traffic go first, and match their speed.
Signal and enter. Other traffic must yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, let other traffic go first, and match their speed.
questions.explanation: Signal and merge smoothly. Match the speed of traffic already on the freeway. Let other vehicles go first.

questions.question: When can you go through a yellow light?

options.text: When an emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
When you are already in the intersection as it turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are already in the intersection as it turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If you are in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you may continue through carefully. Do not enter the intersection on a yellow light.

questions.question: You reach an intersection but are not in the correct lane to turn. What should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your blinker and turn from your current lane.
Go to the next intersection and turn there.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go to the next intersection and turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make a sudden turn from the wrong lane. Drive to the next intersection where you can turn from the correct lane.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with siren and flashing lights is coming toward you. What must you do immediately?

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle, immediately pull to the right side of the road and stop.

questions.question: When making a turn, you must ____ your speed.
questions.correctAnswerText: Decrease
questions.explanation: Slow down when turning. This helps you stay in your lane and control your vehicle.

questions.question: What is true about emergency vehicles?

options.text: They have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and flashing lights.
They may use loudspeakers to give directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must yield to police cars, fire engines, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using a siren or air horn with red or blue flashing lights. Follow any instructions from the emergency vehicle loudspeaker. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so only move when you are sure the road is clear.

questions.question: Is it safe to stop on railroad tracks for a short time while moving with other vehicles?
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Never stop, stand, or park on railroad tracks. Only cross railroad tracks when your entire vehicle will fit on the other side.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line in the middle of the road mean?

options.text: You may pass if it is safe to do so.
Both lanes travel in the same direction.
You may pass even if it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A dashed yellow line means you can pass in both directions if it is safe. Only pass if oncoming traffic will not be affected.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Right turns are not allowed.
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign that drivers must obey. It means right turns are not allowed at this location.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in foggy weather?

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Drive no faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: You must use headlights when visibility drops to 500 feet or less. Use low beams in fog or rain. High beams reflect light back into your eyes and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What should a driver do when entering interstate traffic from an entrance or acceleration ramp?

options.text: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume other drivers will make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
questions.explanation: When entering the interstate from an entrance or acceleration ramp, yield to drivers already on the highway. Merge safely when there is a gap in traffic.

questions.question: What should you do on slippery roads?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit with caution.
Do not drive faster than 20 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you see rain, snow, or sleet. These conditions make roads slippery. Safety may require driving slower than the posted speed limit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a traffic signal is coming up ahead.

questions.question: What should you do if an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you?

options.text: Speed up to get out of the way.
Stop immediately and block the emergency vehicle.
Make every effort to clear a path for the emergency vehicle.
Signal when it is clear for them to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make every effort to clear a path for the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is nearby, do everything you can to give it a clear path. If safe, pull to the side of the road to let it pass.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with care.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop and proceed when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with care.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means caution. Slow down, look both ways, and proceed carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: When you see an accident ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Stay focused on your own driving.
Stop only if you are involved or if emergency help has not arrived yet.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not stop at an accident unless you are involved or emergency help has not arrived. Stay focused on driving and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Do not drive to accidents, fires, or disasters just to look.

questions.question: When is it legal to text while driving?

options.text: At any time if you are under 18.
At any time if you are 18 or older.
If you can text without looking at your phone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only in emergencies.
questions.explanation: You cannot text while driving except in emergencies. Taking your eyes off the road, even for a moment, increases the chance of a crash.

questions.question: An intersection has no traffic signs or signals. You and a vehicle to your right arrive at the same time. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get through first.
Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
Drive through and make the other vehicle stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. Let that vehicle pass safely, then you may go.

questions.question: You are driving on a highway with two solid yellow lines dividing the lanes. What can you do?

options.text: Cross these lines only to turn left into an alley, private road, or driveway.
Cross these lines to pass other vehicles if there is no oncoming traffic.
Cross these lines only to make a U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross these lines only to turn left into an alley, private road, or driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass in either direction. You can only cross them to turn left into an alley, private road, or driveway.

questions.question: When can you cross a dashed white line?

options.text: When it is safe to change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes going the same direction. You can cross them to pass or change lanes if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
Look for a way around any lowered gates.
Assume no train is coming and drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs alert you that a train may be nearby. Always obey these signs. Never go around barriers or ignore the warning.

questions.question: Only vehicles with disability plates or placards can park in spaces marked for people with disabilities.
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Spaces marked "Reserved Parking for Persons with Disabilities" can only be used by vehicles with disability license plates, Disabled Veteran plates, or disability placards.

questions.question: If you stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until you can clearly see all tracks before proceeding.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go through as soon as the train passes.
Go through when one track is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can clearly see all tracks before proceeding.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with multiple tracks, do not move until you have a clear view of all tracks. Even with one track, check again after a train passes because another train may be coming.

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, what must other drivers account for?

options.text: Heavy trucks need more distance to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Heavy trucks need more distance to stop.
questions.explanation: Heavy trucks require more distance to stop than smaller vehicles. Stay where the truck driver can see you and where your view is not blocked by the truck.

questions.question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do?

options.text: Drive slowly so vehicles and pedestrians have time to move.
Honk your horn so vehicles and pedestrians know you are coming.
Stop and make sure no pedestrians or vehicles are coming before you go.
Ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and make sure no pedestrians or vehicles are coming before you go.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the street from a driveway. Yield to any approaching vehicles or pedestrians. Stop before crossing the sidewalk. Not stopping is illegal.
